I am 69 years old. I never went to school, not one day. My father taught me farming when I was 19, and I have worked the land for 50 years. I have 57 mu. That is a big piece of land for two people, me and my wife, so I hire machines for plowing and harvesting. I cannot do the heavy work myself anymore. I grow wheat and maize on 50 mu, planting one after the other. The other 7 mu I plant with scallion. I do what I did last year because last year was okay. If I change something and it fails, I lose money. I watch my neighbor Lao Zhang. He uses about the same amounts as me. If he puts more fertilizer, I put more too. I think about my whole purse — if I spend too much on fertilizer, I have less for hiring the harvest machine. But I would still rather waste some fertilizer than see my crops turn yellow. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting fertilizer is just a cost.

For the wheat on 50 mu, I sowed it last October with improved seed, the same kind everyone in the village uses. Before sowing, I hired a tractor with a rotary tiller to turn the soil after the maize stalks were chopped. I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that is 50 kg. Now in spring, when the wheat turns green, I will spread 75 kg of ammonium bicarbonate per mu. When the wheat starts to joint, I will spread another 50 kg of ammonium bicarbonate. That gives me about 29 kg of nitrogen per mu. The compound fertilizer also gives me about 8 kg of phosphorus and 8 kg of potassium. I will irrigate three times: at green-up, at jointing, and when the grain is filling. I will spray four times: herbicide once, insecticide twice, and fungicide once if I see spots on the leaves. I expect about 550 kg per mu.

For the maize, I will plant 50 mu right after wheat harvest in June. I use the 605 hybrid seed — the one with the big ears. I will not plow the field after wheat. I use the machine to sow directly into the wheat stubble. It saves time and diesel. I will put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing. When the maize is about waist-high, I will spread 30 kg of urea per mu. That gives me about 22 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus 8 kg of phosphorus and 8 kg of potassium from the compound. I will irrigate two times: once at sowing if the soil is dry, and once when the tassels come out. I will spray three times: herbicide once and insecticide twice for the worms. I expect 600 kg per mu.

For the scallion on 7 mu, I will plant it in spring. I use improved seed from the dealer in town. I will rotary till the soil very fine because scallion roots are thin. I will put 80 kg of chicken manure per mu and one bag of compound fertilizer. Then I will add 40 kg of urea and 20 kg of potassium fertilizer later. That gives me about 30 kg of nitrogen, 10 kg of phosphorus, and 18 kg of potassium per mu. Scallion needs a lot of water, so I will irrigate five times. I will spray pesticide five times because insects love the leaves. I expect 4000 kg per mu.
